messages:
emily (Support): FYI ACME reported a sharp drop in embeddings vectors/sec (~60% lower) starting ~03:15 UTC. tokens/sec look steady. They also saw intermittent 400 Unauthorized earlier around 03:10 but retries succeeded. Can ENG investigate and confirm root cause? tagging @james @maria
emily (Support): Paste of sanitized client report: they send batches of ~512 short strings to our embeddings endpoint (model reported as redwood-embed-1536). Response codes are mostly 200 but overall vectors/sec is way down. No dimension mismatch error on client.
james (ML Eng): On it. Two quick hypotheses: 1) traffic routed to a quant variant with lower throughput, 2) autoscaler / pool sizing made requests hit smaller pools, 3) batching pattern causing queuing. Can you attach sample request/headers or a short repro?
emily (Support): Sample sanitized request they provided:
```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \u005c
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \u005c
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \u005c
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1536","input":["short text"]*512}'
```
They say client saw a transient 400 with body: `{\"error\":\"invalid api key\"}` at 03:10 then subsequent retries returned 200.
maria (Infra): Looking at infra graphs: at 03:12 we had a partial rollback of a eu-west deployment which bumped traffic into the shared embedding pool. pool-7 queue_depth spiked to ~1100 (baseline <200) between 03:13-03:18.
ryan (SRE): That spike lines up with an autoscaler cooldown we saw (didn't add nodes due to a reserved-capacity check bug). Autoscaler window ran ~03:10-03:20. If traffic shifted to smaller pool and batching increased, we would see lower vectors/sec even if tokens/sec per-request stayed similar.
james (ML Eng): Also check KV cache hit-rate and routing logs. If many requests fell back to quantized variant (q4_0) we expect lower vectors/sec for small-high-batch workloads.
maria (Infra): Confirmed in routing audit: ~27% of requests for that customer were served by variant `redwood-embed-1536-q4_0` in the 03:12-03:18 window. Our perf matrix shows q4_0 is ~1.8x slower for this request profile.
emily (Support): Customer batches big arrays (512). They prefer not to change client. Is batch size causing the issue when combined with the quant variant?
james (ML Eng): Yes — big single-request batches cause serialization/queuing in the continuous-batching layer. For the q4_0 kernel, per-item throughput is lower; combined, vectors/sec decreases even though token generation up to projection step remains similar. Repro I ran locally:
```bash
# quick repro (simulates their pattern)
python repro.py --endpoint https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  --model redwood-embed-1536-q4_0 --batch-size 512 --concurrency 4
# Observed: ~750 vectors/sec (q4_0) vs ~2200 vectors/sec for redwood-embed-1536 (non-quant)
```
maria (Infra): Also noting the 400 Unauthorized earlier — deploy-bot logs show a partial token rotation rollout around 03:09 that misrouted a small percentage of requests causing 400s; rollback at 03:11. That partial rollout and rollback caused a routing wobble.
deploy-bot: deploy: rollout token-rotation v2 started 2024-11-09T03:09Z (partial), rollback executed 2024-11-09T03:11Z
ryan (SRE): Putting timeline together: token-rotation partial -> transient 400s, rollout triggered routing redistribution -> traffic bumped to shared pool -> autoscaler cooldown prevented scale up -> some requests hit q4_0 variant -> large client batches + quant kernel caused vectors/sec collapse. 400s were a side-effect of token rotation; main throughput regression from routing + autoscaler + kernel performance mix.
james (ML Eng): Short-term mitigations: 1) Pin ACME's routing to `redwood-embed-1536` (non-quant) for now. 2) Add routing rule to avoid q4 variants for customers sending single large-batch requests. 3) SRE to patch autoscaler reserved-capacity check to avoid cooldown in similar rollbacks.
maria (Infra): I'll push an immediate temporary routing override for customer ID (pt-acme) and make reserved-capacity autoscale fix a priority. Also enabling higher priority on reserved pool for the account.
emily (Support): I'll update ACME: explain root cause, timeline, mitigations (pinning + priority) and offer a short-term config change if they want. Thanks all :thumbsup:
ryan (SRE): I'll create an incident tracking ticket and follow-ups in incidents channel.
ops-bot: incident-12345 created: embed-throttle-acme; assignees: maria, ryan, james; sev: P2
emily (Support): Leaving note to follow up after autoscaler patch and routing rollback verification.
